summary: Intermittent mid-stream timeouts when client uploads slow chunked payloads; APIGW suppresses flush leading to idle timeout
description:
Issue summary:
Customers using long-running streaming completions intermittently hit mid-stream timeouts (504/408) during uploads with chunked Transfer-Encoding. Failures correlate with slow client upload rates (small chunks spaced >100ms) and large tracing baggage headers on the initial request. The API Gateway appears to suppress backend flushes while buffering request body chunks, leading to an idle period where the ALB/NGINX idle-send timeout fires.

Impact:
- Multiple SentiHealth endpoints experienced repeated streaming terminations during multi-second completion responses; user-facing apps report hung chat sessions and failed saves.
- Affects enterprise customers behind heavy telemetry/tracing proxies. Estimated 2-4% request failure rate during peak for affected endpoints.

Environment:
- Prod cluster in us-east-1 behind API Gateway and external ALB.
- Frontend client uses chunked Transfer-Encoding to stream long user uploads (voice->text preprocessor).
- Requests include large trace baggage headers (~8-12KB) from customer-side service mesh.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Client opens POST /v1/chat with Transfer-Encoding: chunked.
2) Attach X-Trace-Baggage header containing multiple key/value pairs (total headers ~8-12KB).
3) Send initial small chunk, then wait ~120-300ms before sending subsequent chunks.
4) Backend begins producing streaming tokens; after ~10-15s of streaming, connection resets with 504/408.

Observed behavior:
- Gateway logs show request enters APIGW, but there are long gaps in request body arrival. APIGW keeps connection open and attempts to buffer; backend sees stalled writes and then ALB/NGINX reports idle-send timeout.
- No consistent 5xx from serving runtime prior to disconnect; KV cache warmup sometimes coincides with longer response times which exacerbate the idle window.
- TCP-level traces indicate flushes are coalesced at the gateway and not transmitted to client for ~250ms intervals.

Expected behavior:
- Streaming responses should be delivered to the client even when the client uploads slowly, provided the backend continues to flush tokens; APIGW should not delay backend-to-client flushes beyond configured idle-send timeouts.

Logs / traces / evidence:
- APIGW access logs: correlation_id=cor-9a1b2c; status=504; backend_processing_time=14.8s; upstream_time=14.7s.
- ALB logs: Idle_send_timeout reached after 256s of inactivity on the socket (client-side pacing plus gateway buffering).
- Packet capture (pcap) from edge shows client-to-gateway small chunks separated by 120-250ms; gateway holds buffer before forwarding a coalesced write.
- Application runtime logs show normal token generation; no OOMs or model errors.

Hypothesis:
- APIGW proxy buffering + trace-header growth triggers internal flush suppression and write coalescing. When client uploads are slow, the gateway's buffering behavior creates a window with no egress traffic to the client while waiting to aggregate inbound chunks, allowing ALB/NGINX idle timers to fire. Large initial headers increase internal buffering pressure and may make the gateway wait for full request body semantics.

Temporary workaround for customer:
- Reduce trace baggage size (advise SentiHealth to trim or sample tracing headers).
- Switch client to send fewer, larger chunks (e.g., 1KB+) to avoid long inter-chunk gaps.
- Configure retry policy in client to re-open streaming session on short disconnects and resume where possible.

Next steps / action items:
- Support: validate reproducer against staging APIGW to replicate buffering behavior (assigned to Ethan).
- SRE: review gateway buffering flags and idle-send timeout configuration; evaluate lowering gateway write coalescing window.
- Infra: gather full pcap on affected connections and produce timeline visualization.
- Product: consider documentation note about chunk pacing and header size recommendations for streaming uploads.
comments: 2026-03-01 10:12 - Maya Patel: Ticket created after SentiHealth reported 2.7% stream fails during heavy telemetry periods. Attached initial access logs and sample headers.

2026-03-01 14:03 - Ethan Zhang: Reproduced locally by running a slow-chunk client against staging APIGW. Observed gateway write coalescing of ~180ms before forwarding. Captured pcap and attached to ticket (s3://redwood-support/pcaps/SUP-63421/).

2026-03-02 09:20 - SRE (Nadia Gomez): Confirmed APIGW has a 200ms coalescing write window enabled for HTTP/1.1 chunked bodies; this interacts poorly with ALB idle-send at 250ms in our config. Suggest testing config change to 50ms in staging.

2026-03-02 13:45 - Ethan Zhang: Deployed modified proxy config (write_coalesce_ms=50) to staging; repro rate dropped from 90% to 4% in our synthetic test. Need to assess perf impact at scale before prod rollout.
2026-03-03 08:05 - SentiHealth (Alice Moreno): Confirmed changes in staging help; asked if there are recommended header-size limits to avoid future problems.

2026-03-04 16:30 - Maya Patel: Advised SentiHealth to keep tracing baggage under 6KB and to batch client chunks of >=1KB where possible. Opened a doc PR for guidance: https://confluence.redwood/s/reproducible-streaming-guidance.
2026-03-05 11:00 - Nadia Gomez: Scheduling a controlled canary of reduced write_coalesce_ms across 10% of prod edge (target: 2026-03-10). Linking SUP-63421 to canary runbook and postmortem if needed.
